task_name: The list and the terminal on the page

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and the diff produces all three in production code. (a) 'names the live sessions': SessionsPanel.tsx renders one Button per session carrying {session.name}. (b) 'shows the chosen one': `const chosen = sessions.sessions.find((session) => session.id === chosenId) ?? sessions.sessions[0]` feeds <SessionTerminal session={chosen} />, so the first is shown until a name is clicked and the clicked one afterwards (pinned by the stream URL flipping from /sessions/a1/stream to /sessions/b2/stream). (c) 'in every stage': Home.tsx renders <section className="home__sessions" aria-label="Sesiones en marcha"> between the workspace section and the `workflow !== null` block, gated by nothing, which is what D-21 asks for; Home.sessions.test.tsx pins it before a plan is requested and while an implementation runs. The four branches the brief names (Loading, Banner, a Spanish line, the names plus the terminal) are all present.

The TDD line is `it('the live sessions are listed by their names')` — 'two loaded sessions render both names and the first one's terminal'. The test in SessionsPanel.test.tsx feeds exactly two sessions (TWO_SESSIONS = a1/zsh and b2/bash), then asserts findByRole('button', {name: 'zsh'}), getByRole('button', {name: 'bash'}) and getByLabelText('Terminal de la sesión'): the same input, the same expected values, both names plus the terminal. The 'first one's' half of that sentence is pinned by the neighbouring test the plan's **Tests:** list also names, `it('the first session is the one shown')`, which asserts FakeEventSource.last().url === '/sessions/a1/stream'. Nothing in the named assertion is weaker than the written phrase, and it would go red with SessionsPanel.tsx reverted.

The amended task carries no `Contract (path):` block any more; its content survives as the prose sentence `export const SessionsPanel: () => ReactElement`, and the Call site block is kept. Both are honoured name by name: the diff declares `export const SessionsPanel = (): ReactElement => {` — named export, no parameters, ReactElement return — and Home.tsx contains the call site verbatim, indentation included: `<section className="home__sessions" aria-label="Sesiones en marcha">` / `<SessionsPanel />` / `</section>`. No constant, error or exported name is otherwise fixed by the brief. The three literal strings the tests pin ('No se pudo contactar con las sesiones en marcha', 'No hay ninguna sesión en marcha', 'Sesiones en marcha') match production.

Rows the diff bears on, each implemented with the value stated: D-21 (the cabin offers a place to talk in every phase, no phase hides it) — the section is unconditional inside `main`, not gated by `workflow`; P-3 (the page never opens or kills a session) — the panel only reads useLiveSessions and subscribes, there is no POST /sessions and no delete anywhere in the diff; P-5 (@xterm/xterm doubled with vi.mock) — SessionsPanel.test.tsx and Home.sessions.test.tsx both do `vi.mock('@xterm/xterm', () => …)` and SessionTerminal.test.tsx keeps its double; P-8 (Spanish product copy, English everywhere else) — UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE, NO_SESSIONS_MESSAGE, the aria-labels and the banner copy are Spanish, while every identifier, constant name and test name is English. The remaining rows (D-1..D-20, D-22..D-25, P-1, P-2, P-4, P-6, P-7, P-9) are about the backend or later slices and this diff implements nothing that bears on them; none is reopened.

EXEMPLARS: the named exemplar for a component is `frontend/src/app/implement-progress/components/implement-progress/ImplementProgress.tsx` — component + .css + index.ts beside it, a hook read at the top, message constants at module level, a Banner for the failure branch, BEM class names. SessionsPanel.tsx matches it point for point (SessionsPanel.tsx/.css/index.ts, `useLiveSessions`, UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE/NO_SESSIONS_MESSAGE, `<Banner type="error" role="alert">`, .sessions-panel/.sessions-panel__list/.sessions-panel__empty), the index.ts re-export mirrors session-terminal/index.ts, and SessionsPanel.test.tsx's relative `from './SessionsPanel'` is the exemplar's own idiom (ImplementProgress.test.tsx does the same); the yardstick only forbids climbing `../` imports. Every CSS custom property the new sheets use (--background-elevated, --foreground-secondary, --borderwidth-sm, --border-secondary, --shape-container-sm) exists in src/system-ui/theme/tokens/. The unstyled `sessions-panel__item` class is the host's own habit too (implement-progress__task-name has no rule of its own either), so it is a nit and not charged. REPO RULES: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md — English identifiers and test names, Spanish only for what renders: honoured; no repository control is routed around. frontend/README.md — no semicolons, named exports, one component per file, BEM, no export default, no `../` import: honoured. DEFECTS.MD, RULE BY RULE. (1) Closed vocabulary instead of loose strings and booleans: the panel dispatches over the `status` discriminant of LiveSessionsState ('loading' | 'unavailable' | 'loaded') with three early returns and no catch-all; the last branch is the narrowed 'loaded' member, so adding a member would break `sessions.sessions` at the type checker rather than fall into a default. No boolean stands in for a state. Conforms. (2) No raw map as the return value of logic: no subject that offends — what crosses is the declared `LiveSession[]` from the hook, and the only literal maps in the diff are JSON bodies inside test fetch routers, i.e. the serialization boundary itself. (3) Two fields that have to agree: the only stored state is `chosenId: string | null` and `chosen` is derived on every render (`find(…) ?? sessions.sessions[0]`); the absence of a choice lives in the type as `null` rather than as a sentinel, and no second field repeats it. Conforms. (4) Errors named for what happens, not for where: no subject — the diff raises no error; the single `throw new Error('the recovery banner has not appeared yet')` is a waitFor predicate and is named for what happened. BOUNDARIES/DELIVERY: no boundary is crossed by this diff (the client and the hook arrived in earlier tasks), no signature, constructor or public contract changes, and no call site is left on an old path, so nothing in either yardstick's delivery rules has a subject here. TWO CLASHES DECLARED, NOT CHARGED, as this item's first calibration case asks: (i) `conventions/style.md`'s 'No free function at module level: every function hangs off a type' cannot be satisfied by a component the plan requires to read a hook — `useLiveSessions`/`useState` only work inside a function component, so a class or static method is impossible, and the same holds for the module-level `answering` helper in a Vitest file, which `conventions/testing.md`'s 'test helpers hang off their test type' would want on a test type this framework does not have; every named exemplar is written the same way. (ii) `conventions/testing.md`'s 'an object built by hand in the test when a mother exists' is unsatisfiable for the two-session payload: SessionsMother lives at frontend/src/__scenarios__/SessionsMother.ts, which this task's **Files:** does not carry, so `TWO_SESSIONS` stays inline — the brief now says so explicitly. The same argument covers the xterm MockTerminal now written in three test files: extracting it needs a shared module that **Files:** does not authorise.

Three `-` lines in this diff touch a test's substance, and the task's own text asks for each. (1) SessionTerminal.test.tsx: `-    open() {}` becomes `open(screen: Element) { this.opened = screen }` — the double now records, which is strictly stronger and is what the brief asks for ('Task 7 left terminal.open(screen) unwatched … so the double records what it opened on and a test pins that'). (2) Home.restoreWorkflow.test.tsx: `-    expect(await screen.findByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('Plan arrancado')` becomes the same assertion scoped inside the 'Progreso del plan' region, and the REPO assertion is re-expressed against that same element — same expected values, plus a containment the old form did not require. (3) Home.startPlan.test.tsx: `-    expect(await screen.findByRole('alert')).toHaveTextContent('No se pudo contactar con el backend')` becomes the same assertion scoped inside `.home__recovery`. Both are the 'one assertion the second live region made ambiguous is scoped to its container. None weakens' the brief declares, and both are necessary because the panel's own alert/Loading is now a second live region on the page. Every other `-` line in the seven touched suites is a fetch-router rewrite adding the `/sessions` route (or an import gaining `within`), and in each helper the new route is placed before the delegation, so the inner mocks the call-count assertions read (`expect(fetching).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`, the '/active-plans' filters) never see it and no count changed. No test, case or assertion was removed.

The promised behaviour lives in production code, not in scaffolding. SessionsPanel.tsx (48 new lines) holds the list, the choice and the four branches; Home.tsx holds the unconditional section; Home.css holds .home__sessions; SessionsPanel.css holds the layout. Reverting those production lines fails every new test: the panel suite loses its buttons and its terminal, the aria-current test loses its attribute, Home.sessions.test.tsx loses the 'Sesiones en marcha' region, and SessionTerminal.test.tsx's new test finds `opened` still null. The test-side additions (the xterm MockTerminal, the FakeEventSource, the fetch routers, the recording `open`) only stand in for the browser and the backend, which P-5 and the suite's own idiom require; none of them produces the behaviour being asserted.

Inside the declared files, every line traces to a sentence of the task: the component, its css and its barrel; the one import and the four-line section in Home.tsx; the .home__sessions block appended to Home.css without moving a declaration the shell test pins; the `/sessions` route added to each of the seven test routers ('Unconditional means every Home test now fetches /sessions'); the two scoped assertions; the recording `open` in SessionTerminal.test.tsx. Nothing touches the eight existing endpoints, the command a session runs, the second frame kind, or resizing/opening/killing a session — the four things `### Out of scope` names. THE PLAN HUNK, read line by line, is an amendment and it is justified: it adds the SessionTerminal.test.tsx row to §4 and the eight `(modify)` routes to **Files:** (the unavoidable consequence of an unconditional call site — without them the existing Home suites cannot answer /sessions); it folds the `Contract` block into the prose sentence that the diff then honours verbatim and drops a `Current state (Home.tsx, lines 485-490)` quote whose line numbers earlier tasks had already invalidated; it declares MORE tests than before, not fewer (`it('the chosen session is named as chosen for a screen reader')` and the SessionTerminal one); and it collapses five verification commands into two. That last one is the hunk no program checks, so: the three commands dropped (SessionsPanel.test.tsx, Home.sessions.test.tsx, Home.shell.test.ts) are strict subsets of `npm --prefix frontend test`, which is retained and ran green over 52 files and 991 tests — no control was disarmed and no promised test name disappeared. The aria-current attribute and its test are a human-ordered addition declared by this same amendment and serve the objective's 'shows the chosen one'; its burden of proof under conventions/simplicity.md is discharged by a reader who exists (a screen reader user, for whom the Button variant alone says nothing).

Nine new tests: six in SessionsPanel.test.tsx, one in SessionTerminal.test.tsx, two in Home.sessions.test.tsx. DETERMINISTIC: no clock, no date, no randomness, no sleep and no real network — fetch is stubbed per test, EventSource is the FakeEventSource, xterm is doubled per P-5, and nothing reaches the filesystem. ISOLATED: SessionsPanel.test.tsx installs the fake EventSource in `beforeEach` (which resets its static `opened` array) and unstubs globals in `afterEach`; Home.sessions.test.tsx unstubs in `afterEach` and openHome() reinstalls; each test builds its own fetch answer and RTL's cleanup unmounts, so the session subscription is closed and the terminal disposed; no fixed port, file or directory and no order between tests is assumed. VERIFIES REAL BEHAVIOUR: every assertion is on what production renders or on the literal URL production subscribed to; none would survive reverting SessionsPanel.tsx or the Home.tsx section. I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and its testing-anti-patterns.md reference and found nothing in the new tests I can pin to a sentence of either: the assertion on `lastTerminal().opened` is not anti-pattern 1 (it is the argument production passed across the doubled library boundary, and it goes red the moment `terminal.open(screen)` is deleted, which is exactly the hole task 7 left), the doubles carry every member production calls, and the mock setup is far shorter than the tests. ONE FRAGILITY, OBSERVED AND NOT CHARGED because it is neither a breach of the three nor pinnable to a sentence of that skill: in Home.sessions.test.tsx the panel is loaded with SessionsMother.oneSession(), so the page now opens a second FakeEventSource, and `await streamFrame(PlanEventsMother.ready())` reaches `FakeEventSource.last()`. It is correct today and deterministically so — the /sessions answer resolves during the typing of the form, long before the plan-events source is created by the POST — but the test would hang rather than fail cleanly if that order ever inverted.
